Pieter Levels published a list of 3,728 X accounts that he says post automated AI replies, for anyone to block.

In his announcement on November 19, he said he hopes everyone keeps using it, so that his account becomes "a honeypot for AI replies." If they do, he said, accounts he blocks are "blocked by the entire network and they stop being able to reply to anyone."

The list's page has a "Block all AI reply bots" button that hands over a prompt for a browser agent, an AI assistant that can work a logged-in browser. It's the same prompt he posted on X , and it tells the agent to block every name on the list at "about one block every 3 to 5 seconds." He recommends Claude's Chrome extension for it.

> View the post on X

Before the launch, he had warned : "If you write AI replies under my tweets you will now permanently destroy your X account." He says he has since sent the list to X's chief executive "to train their spam models on."

## 3,728, not 10,000+

He had promised "10,000+" accounts. He says he kept only blocks for AI bot replies , "not older random blocks."

The page has since grown to 3,731 accounts. His post and the page both say 498 more are "already suspended" by X, but the page's own data marks 33 of those as suspended. Most of the rest no longer have a username.

Levels says every account comes with evidence. Most listings carry one note: that he blocked the account "without a public reply." The page's footer says flags "are judgment calls, not proof of AI use."

## The way off is an oath

Accounts can appeal , "but you have to solemnly swear to never use AI to reply again in public," Levels wrote. The appeal form asks the account to post an oath declaring that its owner is "of sound mind and human body" and ending: "Should I break this oath, I accept a permanent block by the entire internet."

Levels says the owner of one listed account told him by DM that he uses AI to reply and "will keep doing so."
